findings.description: The "path past the truncation" case only gets truncated when the temp dir is long. On Linux with the default `/tmp` it is not truncated, so the hint is printed paste-ready and the `<repo>` assertion fails. This happens under the Linux gate too.
findings.body:
**This test case only passes on macOS.** The "a path past the truncation" case expects the `<repo>` fallback. On Linux the path stays under the truncation cap, so `WorktreeConfigError` prints the paste-ready form instead.

How the fallback is chosen:
- `sanitizeReason` caps its output at `FAILURE_SUMMARY_CHARS = 300` code points (`src/adapters/capability.utils.ts:63`) and adds no ellipsis.
- `WorktreeConfigError` uses the `<repo>` form only when `sanitizeReason(raw) !== raw`.

The path lengths:
- **Linux, default `/tmp`:** `tempDir('pup-diff-')` gives `/tmp/pup-diff-XXXXXX` (20 chars). The full path is 20 + 1 + 250 + `/.git/config` (12) = **283**, which is ≤ 300. Nothing is truncated, `config === raw`, and the assertions at L1072 and L1075 (`<repo>/.git/config …` and `with <repo> typed by hand`) fail.
- **pup's gate on Linux:** `sandboxRun` sets `TMPDIR` to `/tmp/pup-gate-XXXXXX` (`src/core/sandbox.utils.ts:513-517`). The path comes to **299**, still ≤ 300.
- **macOS:** the test passes only because `realpathSync(tmpdir())` is a long `/private/var/folders/…` path.

One path component can't fix this, because `NAME_MAX` is 255 and a 255-char name under `/tmp` still comes to only 288 characters. Use two components so the path is long on any platform:

```ts
['a path past the truncation', `${'p'.repeat(200)}/${'p'.repeat(200)}`],
// …
mkdirSync(odd, { recursive: true });
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b96809e1a29ab2b273e9530de426120352f7f09d/src/core/git-diff-client.test.ts#L1052-L1075

findings.description: When the path can't be printed as-is and the value is unreadable, the hint reads "…holds characters this message cannot show as they are first (`-C /`: …)". "first" seems to attach to "show as they are" rather than to the unset, in the one case where the order matters. Put the typed-by-hand clause in parentheses or end it with a delimiter.

The new private `shellWord` is a verbatim copy of the private one in `src/core/merge-gate.service.ts:976-979`, doc comment included, and a third variant next to the exported `shellWord` in `src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts:907`. That is a third use (general.md: "no abstraction until third use"). Consider one shared always-quote helper in core.

A repo path containing a backtick passes the `config === raw` guard and is quoted correctly for the shell. But the hint wraps the command in backticks, so copying the text between them gives a cut-off command. Consider sending backtick paths to the `<repo>` form too.

`WorktreeConfigCause` ('file' | 'on' | 'unreadable') spells out 'on' and 'unreadable' again from `worktreeConfigState`'s return type, with nothing linking the two. Consider `type WorktreeConfigState = 'off' | 'on' | 'unreadable'` and `WorktreeConfigCause = Exclude<WorktreeConfigState, 'off'> | 'file'`.

The `WorktreeConfigError` constructor computes `join(dotGit, 'config')` twice (as `config` and as `raw`) and builds `problem`, `unset` and `steps` through nested conditionals. Writing `const raw = join(...)` first and then `const config = sanitizeReason(raw)` would remove the duplicate join.

For `cause === 'file'` the extension is already off, because the extension is now checked first. The hint still tells the operator to run the `--unset-all`, which exits 5 on an absent key when no sparse checkout ran. Consider "then, if the extension is on, …".
